newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Listing of Indonesia BNI to enliven Jakarta bourse.
newsitem.headline: Listing of Indonesia BNI to enliven Jakarta bourse.

text.p: This month's listing of Indonesia's largest state-owned bank, PT Bank Negara Indonesia 1946 (BNI), will enliven the sluggish Jakarta stock exchange, analysts and brokers said.

The issue, whose approach has slowed trading on the Jakarta bourse in recent weeks, is already seven times oversubscribed, an official of lead underwriter PT Danareksa Sekuritas said after preliminary applications were processed last week.
He said the size of the oversubscription was expected to increase sharply during the offer period which opens on Monday and ends on Thursday before the company is listed on November 25.
"It is expected to be heavily oversubscribed as more individual investors are likely to apply during the offer period," he told Reuters last week.
Analysts and brokers said the huge interest was in line with their estimates at the offer price of 850 rupiah (36 cents) per share.
They said BNI stock was already being traded in the grey market at a 10 percent premium.
"I think it could be well in the top 10," Sue Lloyd, research director at PT Nomura Indonesia, told Reuters.
The bank will float around 1.1 billion shares on the Jakarta and Surabaya stock exchanges, making it the largest single listing in Indonesia during 1996.
Some analysts and brokers said the market had previously estimated an offer price at between 750 and 950 rupiah.
"The offer price is definitely cheap and given the fact that it is the single largest government issue this year, I think it will be a success in Jakarta ," Lloyd said.
Brokers last week said many local traders were cashing in recent speculative gains to be ready to subscribe to BNI.
They said BNI's countrywide network and good price earnings ratio were the prime factors for the stock's lure.

A report from Kleinwort Benson Securities (Asia) Ltd last week said the offer price would put the share's price earnings ratio at 8.2 times its 1997 earnings based on analysts' forecasts collected by the underwriter.
Kleinwort Benson estimated earnings for 1997 at 448.7 billion rupiah and 525.1 billion rupiah in 1998 with earnings per share growth 11.9 percent for 1997 and 17.0 percent for 1998.

But after an initial boost, analysts said the BNI listing was not strong enough to make a long-term difference to the foreign-dominated Indonesian market as the issue had received only an average response from overseas investors.

"I don't think (the issue) will be strong enough to spice up the Jakarta market as even with the float of BNI, the index for the next three months is going to be relatively flat," David O'Neil, investment analyst at BZW Niaga Securities, said.

Analysts said all Jakarta shares could be weakened in the new year ahead of the May 1997 general election as many foreign investors remained wary of the impact on the market of any political instability.
However, O'Neil said the impact of any election-related political problems would have only a short-term effect.
"The market will fall on any political instability, but then there is an opportunity to buy stocks because a lot of companies in Indonesia have strong fundamentals," he said. ($1 = 2,330 rupiah)
